mcq.QUESTION_DESC: In an 8-bit Sign-Magnitude system, how is the decimal number -37 represented? (The magnitude of 37 in binary is 0100101).
Using 5-bit Sign-Magnitude, what is the result of adding +9 and -4? (+9 magnitude is 1001, +4 magnitude is 0100).

mcq.OPT_1: a) It is difficult for humans to understand.
mcq.OPT_2:
b) It requires complex hardware to perform addition and subtraction because it requires both an adder and a subtractor, and a magnitude comparator.
.
mcq.OPT_4: d) It uses more bits than Two's Complement
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: What is a major disadvantage of the Sign-Magnitude representation?
Perform the subtraction +7 - +7 in 4-bit Sign-Magnitude. What is the result?
Perform the subtraction +7 - +7 in 4-bit Sign-Magnitude. What is the result?

sq.ANSWER:
a) +17 + (-13) in 6-bit Sign-Magnitude:

  • +17 = 0 10001 (sign bit 0, magnitude 10001)

  • -13 = 1 01101 (sign bit 1, magnitude 01101)

  • Signs are different, compare magnitudes: 17 > 13

  • Subtract smaller magnitude from larger: 10001 - 01101 = 00100

  • Result takes sign of larger magnitude (positive): 0 00100

  • Final Result: +4 = 000100

b) -20 + (-15) in 6-bit Sign-Magnitude:

  • -20 = 1 10100 (sign bit 1, magnitude 10100)

  • -15 = 1 01111 (sign bit 1, magnitude 01111)

  • Signs are same (both negative)

  • Add magnitudes: 10100 + 01111 = 100011

  • This produces a carry-out from the 5-bit magnitude field

  • Result: Overflow - cannot be represented in 6-bit Sign-Magnitude

c) Hardware Challenges of Sign-Magnitude:

  • Multiple Operations Required: The hardware must first check the signs, then decide whether to add or subtract magnitudes

  • Magnitude Comparator Needed: Requires additional circuitry to determine which number has larger magnitude

  • Separate Adder/Subtractor: Needs both addition and subtraction units

  • Complex Sign Determination: Final sign depends on both the operation and which magnitude is larger

  • Inefficiency: This multi-step process is much slower and requires more hardware than Two's Complement, which uses a single adder for both addition and subtraction
sq.QUESTION_DESC:
Sign-Magnitude Addition with Analysis

Perform the following Sign-Magnitude additions using 6-bit representation and analyze the results:

a) Add +17 and -13 in Sign-Magnitude format
b) Add -20 and -15 in Sign-Magnitude format
c) Analysis: What specific hardware challenges make Sign-Magnitude arithmetic inefficient compared to Two's Complement? Explain with reference to your calculations above.

sq.ANSWER:
a) +11 - +11 in 5-bit Sign-Magnitude:

  • Convert to addition: +11 + (-11)

  • +11 = 0 1011 (sign bit 0, magnitude 1011)

  • -11 = 1 1011 (sign bit 1, magnitude 1011)

  • Signs are different, magnitudes are equal

  • Subtract magnitudes: 1011 - 1011 = 0000

  • Result is zero: 0 0000 (positive zero)

b) -8 - +8 in 5-bit Sign-Magnitude:

  • Convert to addition: -8 + (-8)

  • -8 = 1 1000 (sign bit 1, magnitude 1000)

  • -8 = 1 1000 (sign bit 1, magnitude 1000)

  • Signs are same (both negative)

  • Add magnitudes: 1000 + 1000 = 10000

  • This produces a carry-out from the 4-bit magnitude field

  • Result: Overflow - cannot be represented in 5-bit Sign-Magnitude

c) Fundamental Limitations of Sign-Magnitude:

  1. Dual Representation of Zero:

    • Evidence: In part (a), we got 0 0000 (+0)

    • The system can also represent 1 0000 (-0)

    • This complicates zero-checking logic and is mathematically redundant

  2. Complex Overflow Handling:

    • Evidence: Both examples (b) and previous question showed overflow issues

    • Overflow detection is complicated because it depends on both the operation and the signs of operands

    • In part (b), adding two valid numbers (-8 + -8) produced an invalid result due to magnitude overflow

  3. Additional Limitations Evidenced:

    • Inefficient Hardware: As shown in both questions, the need for multiple operations (compare, add/subtract, determine sign) requires complex circuitry

    • Limited Range: The magnitude field has one less bit due to sign bit, reducing the range of representable numbers compared to unsigned binary
sq.QUESTION_DESC:
Perform the following operations using 5-bit Sign-Magnitude representation and identify any special cases:

a) Subtract +11 from +11 (+11 - +11)
b) Subtract +8 from -8 (-8 - +8)
c) Critical Analysis: Identify and explain two fundamental limitations of the Sign-Magnitude representation system evidenced by your calculations.

lq.ANSWER:
a) Addition Operations

i) (+45) + (+27)

Step 1: Convert to Sign-Magnitude

  • +45 = 0 0101101 (Sign 0, Magnitude 0101101)

  • +27 = 0 0011011 (Sign 0, Magnitude 0011011)

Step 2: Perform Addition

  • Signs are same (both positive) → Add magnitudes

  • Magnitude addition: 0101101 + 0011011 = 1001000

  • Check for carry: Result is 7 bits 1001000 (no carry-out)

  • Final sign: Positive (0)

Result: 0 1001000 = +72 ✓

ii) (-68) + (+39)

Step 1: Convert to Sign-Magnitude

  • -68 = 1 1000100 (Sign 1, Magnitude 1000100)

  • +39 = 0 0100111 (Sign 0, Magnitude 0100111)

Step 2: Compare and Operate

  • Signs are different → Compare magnitudes

  • 68 > 39 → Subtract smaller from larger: 1000100 - 0100111 = 0011101

  • Sign of result: Sign of larger magnitude (negative) → 1

Result: 1 0011101 = -29 ✓

iii) (-52) + (-75)

Step 1: Convert to Sign-Magnitude

  • -52 = 1 0110100 (Sign 1, Magnitude 0110100)

  • -75 = 1 1001011 (Sign 1, Magnitude 1001011)

Step 2: Perform Addition

  • Signs are same (both negative) → Add magnitudes

  • Magnitude addition: 0110100 + 1001011 = 1111111

  • Check for carry: Result is 7 bits 1111111 (no carry-out)

  • Final sign: Negative (1)

Result: 1 1111111 = -127 ✓

b) Subtraction Operations

i) (+60) - (+35)

Step 1: Convert to Addition

  • (+60) - (+35) = (+60) + (-35)

  • +60 = 0 0111100 (Sign 0, Magnitude 0111100)

  • -35 = 1 0100011 (Sign 1, Magnitude 0100011)

Step 2: Compare and Operate

  • Signs are different → Compare magnitudes

  • 60 > 35 → Subtract smaller from larger: 0111100 - 0100011 = 0011001

  • Sign of result: Sign of larger magnitude (positive) → 0

Result: 0 0011001 = +25 ✓

ii) (-42) - (+18)

Step 1: Convert to Addition

  • (-42) - (+18) = (-42) + (-18)

  • -42 = 1 0101010 (Sign 1, Magnitude 0101010)

  • -18 = 1 0010010 (Sign 1, Magnitude 0010010)

Step 2: Perform Addition

  • Signs are same (both negative) → Add magnitudes

  • Magnitude addition: 0101010 + 0010010 = 0111100

  • Check for carry: Result is 7 bits 0111100 (no carry-out)

  • Final sign: Negative (1)

Result: 1 0111100 = -60 ✓

iii) (+25) - (+25)

Step 1: Convert to Addition

  • (+25) - (+25) = (+25) + (-25)

  • +25 = 0 0011001 (Sign 0, Magnitude 0011001)

  • -25 = 1 0011001 (Sign 1, Magnitude 0011001)

Step 2: Compare and Operate

  • Signs are different → Compare magnitudes

  • Magnitudes are equal (25 = 25) → Result magnitude = 0

  • Sign determination: When magnitudes are equal and signs different, result is zero

  • By convention, use positive zero

Result: 0 0000000 = +0 ✓

Operation Result Correct? Overflow? Special Cases
(+45)+(+27) +72 ✓ Yes No None
(-68)+(+39) -29 ✓ Yes No Different signs, magnitude subtraction
(-52)+(-75) -127 ✓ Yes No Boundary case: Largest magnitude negative
(+60)-(+35) +25 ✓ Yes No Subtraction via addition
(-42)-(+18) -60 ✓ Yes No Subtraction of positive from negative
(+25)-(+25) +0 ✓ Yes No Dual zero: Result is positive zero
